newsitem.title: VATICAN: Law threatens Catholic Church in Russia, Pope says.
newsitem.headline: Law threatens Catholic Church in Russia, Pope says.

text.p: Pope John Paul forcefully told Russian President Boris Yeltsin on Thursday that a legislative measure to curb the rights of minority religions in Russia threatened the survival of the Catholic Church there.

"This text...would constitute for the Catholic Church in Russia a real threat to the normal development of its pastoral activities and even its survival," the Pontiff said in a letter released by the Vatican.

The bill, entitled "On Freedom of Conscience and Religious Association", would deny legal status to new religious groups for 15 years. It has already been passed by Russia's parliament and must now be signed by Yeltsin in order to become law.

The measure would give higher legal status to those religious organisations that have been in existence in Russia for 50 years, a definition that encompasses the Russian Orthodox Church, Jewish, Islamic and Buddhist groups, but would impose new curbs on religious activities by others.
The Pope decried the fact that the bill excluded Catholicism from the "traditional religions" protected under the law and called for the "legitimate rights of believers" to be protected.

"Your Excellency will understand my worries and my fervent desire...that we can reach a new draft of a text which...would be a guarantor of religious peace in the great Russian nation," the letter said.
